```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Standardize variables
df['Energy_z'] = (df['Energy_value'] - df['Energy_value'].mean()) / df['Energy_value'].std()
df['Waste_z'] = (df['Waste_value'] - df['Waste_value'].mean()) / df['Waste_value'].std()

# Create adjacency matrix
boroughs = df['borough'].unique()
n = len(boroughs)
adj_matrix = np.zeros((n, n))

# Map borough names to indices
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Fill adjacency matrix
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    adj_matrix[i, j] = 1
    adj_matrix[j, i] = 1  # Make symmetric

# Row-standardize adjacency matrix
row_sums = adj_matrix.sum(axis=1)
W = adj_matrix / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

print("Data loaded and adjacency matrix prepared")
```

```python
# Calculate Lee's L for actual data
y = df['Energy_z'].values
x = df['Waste_z'].values
Wx = W @ x
n = len(y)
L_actual = (y @ Wx) / n

# Permutation test
n_perm = 500
L_perm = np.zeros(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    x_perm = np.random.permutation(x)
    Wx_perm = W @ x_perm
    L_perm[i] = (y @ Wx_perm) / n

# Calculate p-value
p_value = (np.sum(L_perm >= L_actual) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)  # +1 for actual observation

print(f"Lee's L statistic: {L_actual:.4f}")
print(f"p-value: {p_value:.4f}")
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Data cleaning
df = df.dropna(subset=['Waste_value'])  # Remove row with missing Waste value

# Verify we have enough data points
if len(df) < 2:
    raise ValueError("Insufficient data after cleaning")

# Standardization
df['Energy_z'] = (df['Energy_value'] - df['Energy_value'].mean()) / df['Energy_value'].std()
df['Waste_z'] = (df['Waste_value'] - df['Waste_value'].mean()) / df['Waste_value'].std()

# Create adjacency matrix
all_boroughs = set(df['borough']).union(set(adj['borough'])).union(set(adj['neighbor']))
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(all_boroughs)}
n = len(all_boroughs)
adj_matrix = np.zeros((n, n))

for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    if row['borough'] in borough_to_idx and row['neighbor'] in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
        j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
        adj_matrix[i, j] = 1
        adj_matrix[j, i] = 1

# Filter to only boroughs with data
valid_indices = [borough_to_idx[b] for b in df['borough'] if b in borough_to_idx]
adj_matrix = adj_matrix[np.ix_(valid_indices, valid_indices)]

# Row-standardize
row_sums = adj_matrix.sum(axis=1)
row_sums[row_sums == 0] = 1  # Avoid division by zero for isolated boroughs
W = adj_matrix / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Calculate Lee's L
y = df['Energy_z'].values
x = df['Waste_z'].values
Wx = W @ x
n = len(y)
L_actual = (y @ Wx) / n

# Permutation test with more iterations
n_perm = 1000
L_perm = np.zeros(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    x_perm = np.random.permutation(x)
    Wx_perm = W @ x_perm
    L_perm[i] = (y @ Wx_perm) / n

p_value = (np.sum(L_perm >= L_actual) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

print(f"Lee's L statistic: {L_actual:.4f}")
print(f"p-value: {p_value:.4f}")
print(f"Number of boroughs analyzed: {len(valid_indices)}")
```
